skill.name: dogfood
skill.description: Use agent-browser to run structured exploratory QA on web applications. It navigates pages, captures evidence, checks console output, and writes reproducible issue reports.
skill.summary: Run browser-based exploratory QA and produce reproducible web app issue reports.
skill.author: vercel-labs

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown backtick false positives in the taxonomy and instructional prose. Confirmed risks remain where the skill runs agent-browser and shell commands with user-supplied values, captures screenshots or videos, and stores authenticated browser state locally. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Validate target URLs, session names, and output paths. Quote every shell argument or use structured command APIs instead of interpolated Bash examples.

remediation.issue: Credentials and auth state can be exposed
remediation.suggestion: Avoid passing passwords on command lines. Store auth-state.json outside shareable report output, mark it sensitive, and document cleanup steps.

remediation.issue: Screenshots and videos can contain private data
remediation.suggestion: Add clear user consent, redact secrets before sharing, and warn users to inspect all evidence files before distribution.

remediation.issue: Command examples exceed the declared tool scope
remediation.suggestion: Either remove mkdir, cp, and sleep shell examples or declare the required tools clearly so installers can enforce accurate permissions.

content.user_title: Test Web Apps With Repro Evidence
content.value_statement: Web app issues are hard to fix when reports lack proof. This skill explores the app in a browser and creates reproducible evidence for each finding.
actual_capabilities: Opens a target web app with agent-browser and creates a named test session.
Captures annotated screenshots, browser snapshots, console output, and browser errors.
Records repro videos for interactive issues and step-by-step screenshots.
Uses a severity taxonomy for visual, functional, UX, content, performance, console, and accessibility issues.
Writes a structured Markdown report with issue counts, repro steps, and evidence paths.
Saves browser state after login when authenticated testing is required.
limitations: Requires the agent-browser CLI and browser automation access.
Tests observed browser behavior, not the target app source code.
Authenticated testing depends on user-provided credentials or OTP codes.
Evidence files can contain sensitive page data and need careful handling.

use_cases.title: Pre-release exploratory QA
use_cases.description: Run a structured pass across launch-critical flows and produce evidence that engineers can reproduce quickly.

use_cases.title: Regression bug hunting
use_cases.description: Check important pages after a release candidate changes navigation, forms, or stateful workflows.

use_cases.title: UX quality review
use_cases.description: Find confusing flows, missing feedback, visual defects, and accessibility issues from a user viewpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Quick app check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner pass on a local or staging app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Dogfood http://localhost:3000 and create a report in ./dogfood-output.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on one workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Targeted review of a high-priority feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Dogfood https://staging.example.com with focus on onboarding. Capture evidence for every issue and summarize severity counts.

prompt_templates.title: Authenticated product review
prompt_templates.scenario: Testing behind a login with user-provided credentials.
prompt_templates.prompt: Dogfood https://app.example.com. Sign in with the test account I provide, then test account settings and team management.

prompt_templates.title: Release readiness audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced pass across multiple critical areas.
prompt_templates.prompt: Dogfood https://preview.example.com. Prioritize billing, invitations, and project creation. Record videos for interactive failures and use clear repro steps.

output_examples.input: Dogfood http://localhost:3000 with focus on onboarding.
output_examples.output: A Markdown report lists each onboarding issue with severity, category, affected URL, screenshots, and reproducible steps.

output_examples.input: Test the staging billing page after login.
output_examples.output: The report includes billing workflow findings, console errors, annotated screenshots, and videos for interactive failures.

output_examples.input: Run a broad QA pass on the preview deployment.
output_examples.output: The final summary provides total issues by severity and highlights the most important fixes before release.

best_practices: Use test accounts and seed data that can be safely changed.
Review screenshots and videos for sensitive information before sharing them.
Keep the scope clear so exploration focuses on important workflows.
anti_patterns: Running the skill against production with real customer data without approval.
Treating the generated report as a substitute for automated regression tests.
Sharing the output directory before removing secrets, tokens, or private user data.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a Markdown QA report with issue details, severity counts, repro steps, screenshots, and videos when needed.

faq.question: Does it read the target app source code?
faq.answer: No. The workflow tests visible browser behavior and explicitly avoids reading the target application source code.

faq.question: Can it test authenticated apps?
faq.answer: Yes. The user must provide test credentials or OTP codes, and output artifacts should be handled as sensitive.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when the required browser automation tooling is available.

faq.question: What kinds of issues does it look for?
faq.answer: It looks for visual, functional, UX, content, performance, console, and accessibility problems.

faq.question: Is the output safe to share?
faq.answer: Review it first. Screenshots, videos, console logs, and auth state can include private data or session information.
